vocabulary.meaning_en: using the wrong word that sounds similar to the right one
vocabulary.example: Saying "affect" instead of "effect" is a common malapropism.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a word that sounds the same as another but is spelled differently
to change or make a difference to something (the action)
vocabulary.example: How is the medicine affecting her?

vocabulary.meaning_en: the result; what happens in the end
vocabulary.example: The effect of the medicine was good: she felt better.

vocabulary.meaning_en: Latin: to make or do (perfect, defect, affect, effect)
vocabulary.meaning_ar: جذر لاتيني بمعنى يصنع أو يفعل
vocabulary.example: Perfect means made with no mistakes.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a fault; something wrong with a product
vocabulary.example: The phone had a defect, so I returned it.

vocabulary.meaning_en: seeing someone's pain and feeling sorry for them
vocabulary.note_ar: S = subject: أنت تشعر بالأسف لأجله لكنك لا تعيش ألمه
vocabulary.note_en: S = subject: you feel sorry, but you don't feel their pain.
vocabulary.example: I have sympathy for people who lose their jobs.

vocabulary.meaning_en: feeling and experiencing the emotions of another person
vocabulary.note_ar: E = experience: تشعر بما يشعر به
vocabulary.example: I broke my arm once, so I have empathy for him.

vocabulary.meaning_ar: جذر يوناني بمعنى الشعور أو المعاناة
vocabulary.example: Sympathy, empathy and apathy all contain "pathy".

vocabulary.meaning_en: having no feeling or interest in anything
vocabulary.example: He seemed apathetic about his exams.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to suggest something without saying it directly
vocabulary.example: Are you implying that I'm lazy?

vocabulary.meaning_en: to reach a conclusion from information or evidence
vocabulary.note_ar: infer تشبه information: تحتاج معلومات لتستنتج. الاسم: inference
vocabulary.note_en: infer looks like information. Noun: inference.
vocabulary.example: From the dark clouds, I infer that it will rain.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a decision or idea you reach after thinking about facts
in a way that one can be used in place of the other
vocabulary.example: Some people use "imply" and "infer" interchangeably, but they are different.

fine_lines.title: affect vs effect
fine_lines.explanation_ar: affect فعل يعني يؤثّر (A = action). effect اسم يعني النتيجة أو الأثر (E = end).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Affect is a verb: to change something (A = action). Effect is a noun: the result (E = end).

examples.sentence: The cold weather affects my mood.
The cold weather has a bad effect on my mood.

fine_lines.title: sympathy vs empathy
fine_lines.explanation_ar: sympathy: ترى ألم الشخص وتشعر بالأسف لأجله (غالبًا للأشياء السلبية). empathy: تعيش مشاعره وكأنك مكانه، سلبية كانت أو إيجابية.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Sympathy: you see the pain and feel sorry (usually negative). Empathy: you experience the same emotions, good or bad.

examples.sentence: I have sympathy for you; that must hurt.
I've been there too, so I have empathy for you.

fine_lines.title: imply vs infer
fine_lines.explanation_ar: imply: المتكلم يلمّح دون أن يقول مباشرة. infer: السامع يستنتج من المعلومات والأدلة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Imply: the speaker suggests something indirectly. Infer: the listener reaches a conclusion from information.

examples.sentence: He said my pants were shrinking; he was implying I'm getting bigger.
You're eating more doughnuts, so I infer you're gaining weight.

expressions.meaning_en: Are you suggesting (without saying it) that...?
expressions.example: Are you implying that I made a mistake?

expressions.meaning_en: Based on this information, I conclude...
expressions.example: Her coat is wet. From this, I infer that it's raining.
We all have sympathy for the families.
Sleep has a big effect on your health.

grammar.title: affect (verb) vs effect (noun) in sentences
grammar.explanation_ar: affect فعل فتأتي بعده مفعول به مباشرة: X affects Y. أما effect فاسم يأتي بعد a/the أو صفة، ومعه on: X has an effect on Y.
grammar.explanation_en: Affect is a verb: X affects Y. Effect is a noun, used with a/the and "on": X has an effect on Y.
examples: Noise has a bad effect on my sleep.
What are the effects of this medicine?

questions.question: "The ___ of the medicine was very good."
You feel sorry for someone, but you have never felt their pain. You feel ___.
questions.explanation_ar: sympathy = الشفقة والأسف دون أن تعيش الألم.
questions.explanation_en: Sympathy = feeling sorry without feeling their pain.

questions.question: You had the same injury before, so you really feel his pain. This is ___.
Mr. E said, "Your dryer must be very strong; your pants keep getting smaller." He was ___ that James is getting bigger.
"I see wet umbrellas, so I ___ it's raining."
A teenager who doesn't care about anything is ___.
What does the Latin root "-fect" mean?
Choose the correct sentence.
choices: The rain had a big effect on the match.
The rain had a big affect on the match.
The rain affect the match yesterday.
questions.explanation_ar: have an effect on مع الاسم effect.
questions.explanation_en: "Have an effect on" uses the noun effect.
